holds.name: node
holds.reason: engines.node is the consumer compatibility floor of create-modern-cmdk (>=26.4.0 through its 1.x) and the toolchain floor of the monorepo root (engines.node there); modern-cmdk-codemod (the codemod's own package since 1.5.0) declares engines.node >=26.4.0 too (D14), while the deprecated modern-cmdk bin shim states the same floor in its --help instead of an engines field; a library cannot require an exact or pre-release Node. modern-cmdk no longer declares engines (D14, 1.4.0): dropping engines overrides the #42 hold, with evidence (roadmap 1.4.0 risks). The dev toolchain pin is .nvmrc 28.0.0-nightly20261104d36e9ba1f8 (Node 28 nightly), and CI tests both the floor (26.4.0) and 28.0.0-nightly20261104d36e9ba1f8.
holds.evidence: orchestrator decision 2 (2026-10-30); D14 (DECISIONS.md: engines dropped from modern-cmdk only in 1.4; clarified in G-27: the codemod states Node >= 26.4.0 in --help, pinned by tests/unit/codemod-cli.test.ts); engines.node in the root package.json, packages/create-modern-cmdk/package.json and packages/modern-cmdk-codemod/package.json (tests/dist/manifest.test.ts pins the last), and .nvmrc; tests/dist/manifest.test.ts asserts modern-cmdk has none

holds.name: typescript
holds.reason: vue-tsc 3.3.14 (peer typescript >=5.0.0) type-checks the docs app and drives the TypeScript 5/6 compiler API from the package's main export; the typescript 7.x package (latest 7.0.2, next 7.1.0-dev.20261105.1) exports only ./lib/version.cjs at "." plus the new typescript/sync, typescript/async, typescript/ast and typescript/proto API, which vue-tsc and twoslash 0.3.9 do not use. 6.0.3 is the newest 6.x release. Re-test on every sweep: the hold ends when vue-tsc runs on the typescript 7 API.

holds.name: create-modern-cmdk scaffold pins
holds.reason: A scaffolded consumer app pins the npm latest dist-tag of each dependency, never a pre-release channel: the workspace catalog pins experimental React (0.0.0-experimental-e84e1492-20261031) and a TypeScript dev build (7.1.0-dev.20261105.1), which a consumer app must not inherit (SEC-13). This deviates from newest-on-any-channel on purpose. W6-01 re-resolves the pins at the release candidate.
holds.evidence: pnpm view <pkg> dist-tags.latest on 2026-11-05: react 19.3.1 (experimental 0.0.0-experimental-e84e1492-20261031, canary 19.3.0-canary-e84e1492-20261031), react-dom 19.3.1 (same channels), radix-ui 1.8.1 (next 1.8.2-rc.1791984254107), typescript 7.0.2 (next 7.1.0-dev.20261105.1, beta 7.1.0-beta), vite 8.3.6 (beta 8.3.0-beta.1), @vitejs/plugin-react 6.2.1, @types/react 19.3.0, @types/react-dom 19.3.0

holds.name: recast
holds.reason: recast 0.24.0 (latest) is not adopted through a pnpm override. jscodeshift 17.4.0 declares recast ^0.23.11, so every consumer of modern-cmdk-codemod installs recast 0.23.x whatever this repository overrides (an override in pnpm-workspace.yaml never reaches a published manifest): an override would run the fixture suite on a recast that the published codemod never loads, and the modern-cmdk tarball (which bundles it) would differ from the modern-cmdk-codemod tarball. W1-01's probe found nothing in 0.24.0 that printOptions relies on changed (options.js byte-identical; nodeStr, getPossibleRaw, swapQuotes and lines.js unchanged), so the hold ends when jscodeshift releases a version whose range admits 0.24.x.
holds.evidence: pnpm view jscodeshift@17.4.0 dependencies.recast = ^0.23.11 and pnpm view recast dist-tags.latest = 0.24.0 (2026-11-05); pnpm why recast: one version, 0.23.21, reached through jscodeshift 17.4.0 and @types/jscodeshift 17.3.0 (recast ^0.23.11); W1-01 probe of the packed recast 0.24.0 (DECISIONS.md, W1-01 entry, 0208fdd)
